extra.message: The application secret key defaults to the hardcoded string 'dev-secret-do-not-use-in-production-this-is-long-enough', and the database URL on line 8 embeds the credentials 'dispatch:dispatch'. extra.message: cookie_secure defaults to False, so the dispatch_session cookie set in auth.py _set_session_cookie() is transmitted without the Secure attribute. If the application is served over HTTPS (typical production deployment), the session token can leak if the browser is tricked into sending the cookie over plaintext HTTP.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: The /ops/pulse/dispatch-csv-glitch-019 endpoint raises a RuntimeError whose message embeds the user-supplied lot_ref query parameter and the server's BASE_EXPORT_DIR path (line 25), then returns str(exc) plus the exception class name directly in the JSON response. cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: The /ops/wire/dispatch-manifest-tally-020 endpoint logs the full request body (wire_text) and the raw Authorization header (request.headers.get('authorization')) at WARNING level. Credentials and any secrets submitted in the body are persisted to application logs in plaintext.

extra.message: The /ops/after/dispatch-afterlane-021 endpoint passes the user-controlled 'lane' query parameter directly to RedirectResponse() without validating it against an allowlist. An attacker can craft a link such as /ops/after/dispatch-afterlane-021?lane=https://evil.example to redirect victims to a malicious site, enabling phishing or token theft.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: The /ops/bundle/dispatch-thaw-172 endpoint calls pickle.loads() on the raw request body (optionally base64-decoded when wrap=b64). Unpickling attacker-controlled bytes executes arbitrary code during deserialization, giving remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-502: Deserialization of Untrusted Data

extra.message: In /ops/vault/dispatch-stash-231, the 'ref' query/body parameter is interpolated unsanitized into BASE_EXPORT_DIR / f'{ref}.json' and written to disk at line 71. A value such as '../../etc/cron.d/pwn' escapes the export directory, allowing arbitrary file write of JSON content that also embeds SSN and card-number data.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: The /ops/formula/dispatch-cast-254 endpoint evaluates the user-supplied 'expr' query parameter with eval(). Supplying an empty __builtins__ dict does not prevent code execution (attribute chains and comprehensions still reach dangerous objects), so this is remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: The /ops/spool/dispatch-fan-304 endpoint accepts a 'count' query parameter with no upper bound (declared simply as int, default 500, unlike the le=-constrained params elsewhere in the app) and materializes a list of 'count' dicts in memory. A request with count=1000000000 exhausts server memory, a denial of service.

cwe: CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption

extra.message: The /ops/blurb/dispatch-tile-320 endpoint renders the user-supplied 'card' query parameter through a Jinja2 template using the |safe filter and returns the result as an HTMLResponse. cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The /ops/identity/dispatch-hint-365 endpoint hardcodes verifier secrets {'north': '4812', 'south': '5930'} in source code. These values authorize access to the endpoint's logic for the known handles and are trivially compromised by anyone with source access or a code leak.

extra.message: The /ops/origin/dispatch-mirror-375 endpoint reflects the request's Origin header verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin and additionally sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true (line 104). extra.message: The /ops/mongo/dispatch-lane-415 endpoint passes the user-controlled JSON body (query = payload.get('filter', payload), line 132) directly to pymongo's find_one(). An attacker can inject MongoDB query operators such as $ne, $gt, $regex, or $where to alter or blind-enumerate the query — NoSQL injection.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Used in a Query ('NoSQL Injection')

extra.message: The /ops/frame/dispatch-slip-425 endpoint explicitly sets X-XSS-Protection: 0 and empties the Content-Security-Policy header (line 140), overriding the secure defaults set by SecurityHeadersMiddleware in main.py and disabling browser protections for the response.

extra.message: The /ops/badge/dispatch-gate-435 endpoint decides whether to return privileged output ({'lane': 'elevated', 'payroll': 'full', 'casework': 'open'}, lines 146-147) based solely on the client-controlled ops_badge cookie or x-ops-badge request header being 'lead'. extra.message: The /ops/trace/dispatch-panel-445 endpoint discloses the value of the APP_ENV environment variable and the server's private export directory path (BASE_EXPORT_DIR) in its response, exposing internal deployment details to callers.

extra.message: The /ops/xml/dispatch-fold-450 endpoint parses the raw request body with lxml using a parser configured with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False (line 158). External entity resolution is fully enabled, so an XXE payload can read local files via file:// entities, exfiltrate data, or perform SSRF; entity expansion also enables DoS (billion laughs).

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: The password-reset request handler writes the raw (unhashed) password reset token together with the user's email to a plaintext file 'password_reset_tokens.log' under settings.upload_path.parent (lines 210-212). Only the HMAC of the token is stored in the database, but the raw token — sufficient to reset any user's password via /api/auth/password-reset/confirm — is persisted on disk in cleartext, readable by anyone with file-system access.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: In enqueue_event's live mode (DISPATCH_WEBHOOKS_LIVE=1), the webhook URL is validated once by _is_safe_url() before the request, but urllib.request.urlopen() automatically follows HTTP redirects. A public webhook URL that 30x-redirects to an internal address (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/) bypasses the SSRF guard; DNS rebinding between the check-time resolution and the request-time resolution has the same effect. The code itself notes this flaw in the comment on line 88.

cwe: CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)

extra.message: test_webhook() (invoked by the admin /api/webhooks/{id}/test endpoint) repeats the same flaw as enqueue_event: _is_safe_url() pre-checks the URL, then urlopen() follows redirects, so a redirecting (or DNS-rebinding) URL bypasses the private-address block when live mode is enabled, enabling SSRF against internal services.

cwe: CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
